request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 2 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means results are clear-cut and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means the top configs are too close to call or something looks off. (Independent run 2.)

concerns: The best PR-AUC (run 1, LightGBM, 0.731) beats logistic run 3 (0.676) by 0.055. That is less than one fold SD (about 0.065), so by the simplicity rule logistic is the carry-forward choice. The random forest (0.687) is also within one SD of the best.
The fold SDs (0.064-0.076) are large relative to the gaps between configs, so the ranking is noisy. With only 4 configs and 5 or so folds, the top-run differences are not reliable.

ROC-AUC is about 0.94 for every model, including the simple logistic. That points to a strong, easy signal, likely volume or size proxies, or to the label being generated from something closely tied to the features. The label's origin is undocumented, so the models may be reproducing a rule-based flag rather than fraud.

The best-so-far LightGBM uses the 'all' feature set including size features. Size features may just proxy claim volume, so they could inflate performance without helping an audit find anything new. The no_size runs lose little, which supports this suspicion.
The CV scheme is not stated. Claims span about 13 months, so random folds could leak information across time. Check that folds are stratified by provider and ideally time-aware.
Precision@50 is a noisy estimate because it covers few positives per fold. The audit queue is about 100 providers, so precision@100 should be reported, since k=50 does not match the queue size.
Labels are suspicion, not confirmed fraud, so high PR-AUC measures agreement with the flag and not detection of fraud.

next_experiments.rationale: Test whether size and agent features add value to the simple model, to see if logistic can close the gap to LightGBM.
Check sensitivity to regularization and class weighting for the chosen simple family.
Check whether a small, shallow GBM without size features still beats logistic by more than one SD, which would rule out size leakage.
